Nestled in the northwest corner of Hanoi’s historic Old Quarter, Hang Vai Street stands as a testament to the enduring charm of traditional Vietnamese craftsmanship. Once a vibrant marketplace for dyed fabrics, the street now thrives as a bustling hub for bamboo and rattan products, reflecting a transformation that mirrors the dynamic evolution of Hanoi itself.

Today, Hang Vai Street is renowned for its array of bamboo and rattan products, ranging from sturdy bamboo ladders to simple smoking pipes called “điếu cày.” The street’s visual landscape is dominated by towering stacks of green bamboo poles and rattan canes, creating a striking contrast against the weathered, moss-covered walls of the traditional “nhà ống” buildings that line the narrow thoroughfare.
